The row now reads 'For an AR(1) series with \(\phi \gt 0\), the iid bootstrap understates the standard error of the mean by \(\sqrt{(1+\phi)/(1-\phi)}\)', grade T, 'Derived in section 3'. Re-derived: for x_t = phi x_{t-1} + e_t, |phi| < 1, gamma(h) = sigma^2 phi^|h|/(1 - phi^2), so sum_h gamma(h) = sigma^2/(1-phi)^2 and the ratio of the long-run to the iid variance gamma(0) is (1+phi)/(1-phi) (section 3 displays exactly this chain). The iid bootstrap variance of the mean is gamma-hat(0)/T, so true SE / iid SE = sqrt((1+phi)/(1-phi)): 1.732 at phi = 0.5 (ratio 3), 1.5275 at 0.4, exactly 1 at phi = 0 (no understatement, hence the strict inequality is right), and 0.577 at phi = -0.5 (ratio 1/3), where the iid value is 1.73 times too large. For phi > 0 the ratio exceeds 1 because 1 + phi > 1 - phi, so 'understates' holds for every phi in (0, 1): the row is now exactly true in its stated domain. The quoted factor is the large-T limit that section 3 displays (T Var(x-bar) -> ...); at T = 500 and phi = 0.5 the exact finite-sample factor is sqrt(2.992) = 1.730 against 1.732 (2.992 = 3 - 1/125, the T Var(d-bar) printed by Problem E4), so the table is right as an asymptotic statement and consistent with the page's own T = 500 numbers. Every other place on the page that says 'understates' is conditioned: section 3 text at phi = 0.5, the figure caption 'With positive autocorrelation (phi > 0)', M3 (phi in {0, 0.3, 0.5, 0.6}), quiz item 5 (phi = 0.5), and Remark 3.5 ('with phi gt 0'); a grep of L03, L04, index.html and cards.json for 'understate' finds no other unqualified AR(1) claim. Introduction, p. 1: 'Over the original period (1975 to 2006), we show that reasonable adjustments to the parameter choices made by BSW and AP result in a sizeable reduction in the bias relative to AP. Over the updated period (1975 to 2018), we show that the performance of the FDR improves dramatically across a large range of parameter values. Body, p. 2: 'BSW and AP study the period 1975 to 2006'; 'Using the same procedure as in BSW and AP, we find that the probability of misclassifying a fund with an alpha of 2% per year drops to 37%. rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L03.html Lemma 2.3 (line 102) and its proof; card S7-c217
rows.evidence: unchanged since 584f614 (git diff checked); round-12 evidence: Re-derived. (a) p_(k) <= kq/m iff at least k p-values are <= kq/m: if p_(k) <= kq/m then p_(1..k) are all <= kq/m, so N(k) >= k; if N(k) >= k then the k-th smallest is <= kq/m. Hence R = max{k : N(k) >= k}. (b) If R >= 1, a rejected H_i has p_i <= p_(R) <= Rq/m. Conversely, if p_i <= Rq/m but p_i = p_(j) with j > R, then p_(j) <= Rq/m <= jq/m, so N(j) >= j, contradicting the maximality of R; the zero case is handled (N(1) >= 1 forces R >= 1). (c) Raising a p-value can only lower each N(k), so the largest k with N(k) >= k cannot increase. Numerical spot check (scratch py/spotchecks_r12.py): for 2,000 random p-vectors (m = 10, q = 0.05, mixed scales) the BH rejection set equals {i : p_i <= R q/m} with R = max{k : N(k) >= k} (0 violations), and R does not increase when one randomly chosen p-value is raised (0 violations). Ties: the proof uses the k-th smallest p-value, so ties do not change the count.

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L03.html Proposition 5.3 (line 281) and its proof; card S7-c218
rows.evidence: unchanged since 584f614 (git diff checked); round-12 evidence: Re-derived for rho in [0,1). Given z_i = t, the joint Gaussian (W, z_i) gives W | z_i = t ~ N(sqrt(rho)(t - mu_i), 1 - rho), stochastically increasing in t for rho >= 0 (the constant case rho = 0 is trivially monotone). The other coordinates are z_j = sqrt(rho) W + sqrt(1-rho) eps_j + mu_j with eps_j independent of (W, z_i), so P(z in D' | z_i = t) = E[g(W) | z_i = t], g non-increasing for a decreasing D' (translating all z_j by a common amount). Hence t -> P(z in D' | z_i = t) is non-increasing, which is PRDS (Definition 5.1) on every subset. Numerical spot check (scratch py/spotchecks_r12.py, Monte Carlo 600,000 draws, rho = 0.5, m = 3, D = {p_2 >= 1/2, p_3 >= 1/2}, an increasing set in p-space): P(D | z_1 near t) falls from 0.556 at t = -1 to 0.033 at t = 2 (non-increasing in t), and P(D | p_1 near u) rises from 0.054 at u = 0.05 to 0.708 at u = 0.95 (non-decreasing in u): the PRDS inequality holds in the numerical check. (An earlier attempt used the z-increasing set {z_2 > 0, z_3 > 0}; that set is not an increasing set of p-values, so it was discarded.)

rows.location: course/modules/S/S7/L04.html line 365 (section 6, the new T span: 'Step 2 of Definition 4.1 recentres every strategy ... never more')
rows.evidence: Derivation (re-derived). Definition 4.1 (L04.html line 268): V_K = max_k sqrt(T) dbar_k; V*_{K,j} = max_k sqrt(T)(dbar*_{k,j} - dbar_k) with ONE stationary index sequence per draw j shared by every strategy; p_hat = B^-1 sum_j 1{V*_{K,j} >= V_K}. Adding strategy K+1 with statistic s = sqrt(T) dbar_{K+1} adds one term to each maximum: V*_{K+1,j} = max(V*_{K,j}, term_j) >= V*_{K,j} pathwise, for ANY added strategy (no condition needed). If s <= V_K then V_{K+1} = max(V_K, s) = V_K, so 1{V* >= V_K} can only switch from 0 to 1 and p_hat rises; rejection {p_hat <= alpha} then implies rejection before. Numerical check, seeded: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify19h-L03-L04-b/py/rc_pathwise.py -> 'trials=400 not-largest additions checked=399 violations=0' and 'raise-each-maximum holds for any added strategy in 200 of 200 trials' (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify19h-L03-L04-b/rc_pathwise.out; the only raw differences were floating-point noise of 2.7e-15 in V_K, see py/rc_debug.py). COUNTEREXAMPLE to the un-qualified last clause ('a poor alternative can make the Reality Check reject less often, never more'): /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify19h-L03-L04-b/py/rc_counterexample.py (/tmp/claude-0/-home-user-quant-phd/cdd15252-4236-59f9-8fa8-e63e41e1dc0d/scratchpad/verify19h-L03-L04-b/rc_counterexample.out): K=1 (sample mean exactly 0) gives V=-0.0000, p_hat=0.5010, no rejection at 10%; adding a path with true mean -0.2 whose realised sample mean is +0.5 (sqrt(T) x mean 8.66, the largest statistic) gives V=8.6603, p_hat=0.0000, rejection. The pathwise statement holds only when the added statistic is not the largest, which the sentence states before the clause; the clause itself does not carry that condition. L04 Problem E3's solution already says the p-value is lower when the noisy strategy sets V_K (L04.html line 622). The span is graded T, so the claim must be exact. Terminology: the sentence says the RC 'recentres every strategy at its own sample mean', while Definition 6.1 (line 369), the Lab 3 code (centre = 0 unless the mean is below -A) and the figure caption (line 439) say the RC recentres at ZERO; the same operation is described in two vocabularies within section 6. Grade and citation of the T span are otherwise right (no citation; the proof is complete on the page).

freshness_flags: Frederiksen, Matsui & Pedersen (2026), 'Heavy Tails and Predictive Ability Testing', arXiv:2605.16866 (still arXiv in a web search today): with infinite-variance loss differentials a nominal 5% predictive-accuracy test may over-reject. Relevant to Theorem 5.1's moment conditions and the L04 canon-breaks. Working paper, grade C at most. Optional: L04 has no debate brief (the S7 curriculum entry has no debate). (Carried.)

Monschang, Trede & Wilfling (2026), 'Multi-Horizon Uniform Superior Predictive Ability Revisited', JBES, DOI 10.1080/07350015.2025.2569479: asymptotic size and consistency of a uniform SPA test across horizons. Optional context for L04 s6/canon-breaks; not counter-evidence to any claim on the page. (Carried.)

Wang, Zhao, Feng & Wang (2025), 'Robust mutual fund selection with false discovery rate control', Journal of Econometrics 252, 106121, DOI 10.1016/j.jeconom.2025.106121: possibly relevant to the BSW vs Andrikogiannopoulou-Papakonstantinou exchange in L03 s7; check before any future debate brief. (Carried.)

Ota (2026), 'Fixed-level calibration of the Cauchy combination test', arXiv:2603.22668 (v1 24 March 2026, revised; no journal reference): the raw Cauchy combination test is generally not asymptotically exact at a fixed level under equicorrelated Gaussian dependence as the number of combined p-values grows. Relevant context for the bouamara2025stepwise span in L04 canon-breaks (StepC builds on the CCT). Working paper, grade C at most; not published counter-evidence, so no change is required now. Re-check for a published version before a future revision.

Chen & Dim, 'High-Throughput Asset Pricing', arXiv:2311.10685 (first posted 2023-11-17, revised 2025-06-02; no journal reference on arXiv): applies empirical Bayes to 136,000 long-short strategies, reports that EB gives unbiased predictions where naive Sharpe-ratio mining does not, and that multiple-testing methods popular in finance fail to identify most out-of-sample performers. Directly relevant to L03 section 7 (Definition 7.7, Proposition 7.8, Lab 4) and to the R2/canon discussion; working paper, grade C at most. (New in round 7.)

Coroneo & Iacone (2025), 'Testing for equal predictive accuracy with strong dependence', International Journal of Forecasting 41, DOI 10.1016/j.ijforecast.2024.11.003 (Crossref checked): the DM test can lose power and over-reject when the loss differential is strongly dependent. Relevant to Proposition 1.3's summability assumption (i) and to Problem E4; L04 has no debate brief, so optional. Harvey, Leybourne and Newbold's (1997) small-sample DM correction is the classic related reference (not in the registry). (New in round 7.)
